3A. Multi-Model Soil Moisture Partitioning (NASA GLDAS)

⚡ Test This Live in Workbench

Open-loop land surface models (Noah 2.1 & VIC 2.1) simulate topsoil moisture (top 2 meters) purely from atmospheric forcing (rainfall, solar radiation, temperature, wind). In the Northwest full record, topsoil drying accounts for only [-0.12, -0.10] cm/yr, leaving a dominant subsurface deficit of [-1.12, -1.11] cm/yr strictly labeled: "groundwater + surface water + model error residual".

Plain-Language Soil Moisture Audit: Land models (GLDAS Noah and VIC) reveal that topsoil moisture (0–2 meters deep) exhibited minimal change (-0.02 to -0.06 cm/yr). This indicates that shallow soil moisture accounts for less than 10% of Northwest water loss—the vast majority (-1.19 to -1.23 cm/yr) is unmonitored residual loss from deep underground reserves and surface storage.

Methodological Quarantine Notice: Catchment Land Surface Model (CLSM 2.2) assimilates GRACE satellite gravity observations via an Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF). Because CLSM directly ingests GRACE data to adjust its soil moisture fields, using CLSM to explain GRACE constitutes circular reasoning. CLSM attributes -0.94 cm/yr to soil moisture, artificially compressing the residual to -0.33 cm/yr. CLSM is quarantined from the independent physical partition.
threeway:
3B. Inter-Satellite Transition Gap Sensitivity (2017–2018)
⚡ Test This Live in Workbench Intercalibration Audit

Between GRACE decommissioning (2017-06) and GRACE-FO startup (2018-06), an upward step offset (+9.15 cm in NW, p = 0.028) of unknown origin is detected in the raw gravimetric anomaly series. Because Monte Carlo red-noise simulations show that an unadjusted step is falsely flagged as a trend in 93.8% to 100% of simulations under standard linear models, multi-satellite linear trends across unbridged gaps must always be reported alongside step-adjusted and buffer-excluded bounds. The Northwest rate is bounded between -1.81 and -1.25 cm/year (lead benchmark: -1.56 cm/year).

Plain-Language Sensor Transition Audit: Between 2017 and 2018, NASA bridged the original GRACE satellite to GRACE Follow-On. All three independent transition tests—analyzing the original satellite era alone (-1.41 cm/yr), mathematically adjusting for the satellite handoff step (-1.25 cm/yr), or cutting out the gap entirely (-1.27 cm/yr)—consistently agree on rapid, sustained water storage loss in the Northwest.

2B. Between-Region Secular Trend Differences (2002–2026)
⚡ Test This Live in Workbench Calibrated Pairwise Tests

Pairwise secular trend differences using Calibrated ESS-MK on the difference series and within-family Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control.

Plain-Language Regional Contrast: Northwest Bangladesh is losing water significantly faster than all other parts of the country (declining -0.70 to -1.21 cm/yr faster than Eastern and Southern regions). Meanwhile, Southwest and Southeast Bangladesh show balanced water storage with no detectable decline, with storage loss observed across the northwestern agricultural basin.

limitations:
6. Scientific Limitations & Master Data Appendix

Upholding strict scientific integrity by documenting observational boundaries and providing the complete 336-test audit database.

Audit Standards
Observational Pattern What It Cannot Prove Resolution Pathway
1. Regional Storage Depletion Coarse gravimetric resolution (~300 km) cannot resolve district, upazila, or municipal drawdown. Satellite radar interferometry (InSAR) ground deformation and sub-basin subsidence modeling.
2. Residual Subsurface Loss Satellites measure total column mass; we cannot separate deep groundwater from surface water bodies without ground well data. Direct integration of BWDB nationwide in-situ piezometer well hydrographs.
3. Agricultural Pumping Link We do not possess direct metered pumping logs across the Barind agricultural tract. Sub-district agricultural power consumption records and deep tubewell discharge registries from the BMDA.
4. Satellite Transition Gap The 11-month transition (2017–2018) between GRACE and GRACE-FO introduces an upward offset (+9.15 cm, p=0.028) of unknown origin. Continuous multi-satellite airborne gravimetry bridging or hydrodynamic data assimilation.
5. Surrogate Placebo Sensitivity On a real-residual surrogate placebo, NW previously showed an elevated False Positive Rate of 17.6% (82.5% CI coverage) under ESS-MK, whereas under independent AR(1) Monte Carlo null test, Calibrated ESS-MK passes nominal standards (4.10% FPR, 95.90% coverage). Both tests are reported to document sensitivity to empirical noise structure; longer continuous records will narrow this uncertainty.
6. Precipitation Latency GPM IMERG Final Run V07B currently extends through September 2025 due to NASA GES DISC latency, truncating the final 10 months. Updating the processing stream when NASA releases late-2025 and 2026 Final Run granules.
7. Descriptive Nature of Divisions Administrative divisions cannot be treated as statistically independent hydrological catchments. Divisions are strictly labeled descriptive; hypothesis tests are evaluated at the 5-region and National scale.
8. Untested Flood Mechanism The hypothesis that topsoil saturation limits deep infiltration during catastrophic floods remains unverified. Direct borehole piezometer infiltration measurements during monsoon flood waves.
Plain-Language Limitations Summary: Satellite gravimetry measures total mass changes across broad regional areas (300 km footprint). It provides clear macro-level evidence of long-term water balance trends, but cannot monitor individual village tubewells or replace on-the-ground well networks.

5. Regional Stakeholder Action Directives

Translating 24-year satellite trend detection into differentiated policy mandates, agricultural directives (Do's & Don'ts), and citizen initiatives.

Policy Guidance
Northwest Depletion Corridor (Rajshahi & Rangpur)
Satellite Metric: -1.25 cm/yr TWS decline (-0.39 km³/yr). Rainfall: No detectable trend (-1.91 mm/yr).

Depletion is consistent with intensive dry-season Boro rice cultivation on Pleistocene clay terraces that impede natural monsoon recharge.

[MANDATE] BMDA & Water Board: Enforce smart-card volumetric pricing and halt unmetered deep tubewell permits. Expand surface water irrigation from Padma/Teesta rivers by 10% by 2030.
[FARMER DO'S]: Adopt Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) using PVC pipes (cuts water use by 15–30%). Plant short-duration drought-escaping T. Aman (BRRI dhan56/57) before July 24. Shift to winter crops (BARI chhola-5, BARI sarisha-10).
[FARMER DON'TS]: Do not maintain continuous standing water in Boro paddies. Do not plant three-crop continuous cereal rotations. Do not delay T. Aman transplanting past July 24.
[CITIZEN ACTION]: Convert upland plots to drought-hardy orchards (mango, jujube, dragon fruit). Install rooftop rainwater harvesting and farm recharge ponds.
Northeast Haor Basin (Sylhet & Mymensingh)
Satellite Metric: -0.56 cm/yr TWS decline. Mean dry-season drawdown: 58.48 cm.

Choked river corridors drain summer flash floods rapidly into the Bay of Bengal, leaving subsurface storage unrefilled for the dry season.

[MANDATE] BWDB & Haor Dev Board: Construct and maintain engineered submersible embankments against early April flash floods. Dredge rivers and raise rural homestead mounds.
[FARMER DO'S]: Plant flash-flood-escaping Boro varieties (BRRI dhan110, 28, 58) for early April harvest. In floodplains, plant submergence-tolerant Aman (BRRI dhan51/52).
[FARMER DON'TS]: Do not plant long-duration Boro (BRRI dhan29) in deep Haor bowls where April floods destroy unharvested crops. Avoid unlined earthen canals.
[CITIZEN ACTION]: Construct floating agricultural beds (dhap) using water hyacinth. Raise pond embankments and install nylon netting to prevent fish loss.
Central Megacity & Terrace (Dhaka Division)
Satellite Metric: -0.47 cm/yr TWS decline. Highest monsoon storage response ratio (42.2%).

Relentless municipal and industrial groundwater extraction from the "Dupi Tila" aquifer formation beneath impervious Madhupur clay creates a deep metropolitan cone of depression.

[MANDATE] RAJUK & DWASA: Enforce Zero-Liquid-Discharge (ZLD) for Gazipur/Narayanganj textile factories. Mandate rooftop Managed Aquifer Recharge ("MAR") in municipal building codes.
[FARMER DO'S]: Practice contour mulching and intercrop pineapple with ginger and turmeric on the Madhupur Tract. Cultivate disease-resistant BRRI dhan114.
[FARMER DON'TS]: Do not irrigate peri-urban vegetables with untreated industrial effluent from the Turag or Buriganga rivers. Do not clear-cut hillocks.
[CITIZEN ACTION]: Establish urban rooftop gardens with rainwater harvesting and greywater recycling to cool buildings and reduce urban runoff.
Southwest Estuarine Delta (Khulna & Barishal)
Satellite Metric: No detectable trend in bulk mass (-0.05 cm/yr), but severe dry-season salinity intrusion.

Reduced dry-season freshwater river flow drives a brackish salinity wedge into shallow subsurface waters and polders, idling agricultural land in winter.

[MANDATE] Coastal Polder Management: Operate coastal polder sluice gates dynamically to trap fresh monsoon river water internally before February salinity spikes. Enforce agro-ecological zoning.
[FARMER DO'S]: Cultivate salt-tolerant Boro rice (BINA dhan10, BINA dhan8, BRRI dhan67). Grow saline-tolerant sweet potato (BARI misti alu-6) on residual moisture.
[FARMER DON'TS]: Do not plant salt-sensitive BRRI dhan28 in coastal mauzas. Do not breach polder embankments for brackish tiger shrimp (bagda) monoculture.
[CITIZEN ACTION]: Construct raised bed-and-trench (Sorjan) systems to block capillary salt rise for vegetable cultivation. Maintain Pond Sand Filters for drinking water.
Southeast Hill Tracts (Chattogram & CHT)
Satellite Metric: No detectable trend in bulk mass (-0.05 cm/yr), but lowest monsoon retention (26%).

Steep Tertiary hill slopes cause 74% of heavy monsoon rain to sheet off instantly as rapid runoff, drying up natural hill springs by winter.

[MANDATE] Hill District Councils: Provide land tenure security and micro-credit for Sloping Agricultural Land Technology (SALT). Legally protect Village Common Forests (VCFs).
[FARMER DO'S]: Implement SALT contour hedgerows using nitrogen-fixing legumes every 4–6 meters to diffuse runoff. Cultivate flash-flood-tolerant BRRI dhan110.
[FARMER DON'TS]: Do not practice short-fallow slash-and-burn or till root crops vertically on steep slopes. Do not expand tobacco farming in river valleys.
[CITIZEN ACTION]: Establish multistrata perennial fruit orchards. Protect headwater bamboo inside Village Common Forests to revive natural springs (chhara).
National Macro-Regional Directives Summary
Satellite Metric: -0.51 cm/yr national TWS decline; 108.5M people live in depleting northern & central regions.

National water management requires a regionalized approach: Northwest replenishment, Northeast flash flood escape, Central industrial water recycling, and Southern salinity barrier management.

[MANDATE] Ministry of Water Resources: Implement the Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 with regional differentiation rather than uniform national water policies.
[FARMER DO'S]: Match crop choices to regional hydrological regimes: drought-tolerant crops in NW, flash-flood-escaping varieties in NE, and salt-tolerant cultivars in SW.
[FARMER DON'TS]: Do not treat water resources as homogeneous across the country; avoid applying uniform dry-season pumping standards nationwide.
[CITIZEN ACTION]: Support community water monitoring, local watershed protection, and rooftop rainwater harvesting across all divisions.
